description: Keeps the main thread thin: a clearly multi-step / implementation-shaped Bash by the orchestrator (chained >2 steps, a heredoc, sed -i/tee, npm/cargo/make build, git commit/push, pytest/test runs, AND almost all `gh` incl. `gh pr`/`gh run`/`gh api`, OR a sanctioned orchestration head chained with an unrecognized segment at any length — `omp-steer 1 x; rm -rf y`, agent-tools#861) warns-then-blocks. A bare >/>> redirect is not implementation on its own. Read-only inspection AND sanctioned orchestration are never blocked, even chained, loops/conditionals included (for/do/done/while/if/then/else/fi are segmentation keywords, stripped and never counted as steps): git status/ls/cat/grep/find/sort/tr/cut/jq, print-only sed/awk, tg, task, review, git worktree list, omp-steer (any args), tg-ctl status|inbox|audit-delivery|ask|omp-live status|send, rig status|doctor (no --yes/--fix/--optional)|sysmon status|sample|incidents|--version, and the read-only gh allowlist. `tg` (ALL tg-cli commands — send text, --file, --photo, --format html, --tag, --reply-to, voice setup, everything, per Alex's direct authorization) matches on a bare `tg` head only (optionally with a leading VAR=val env prefix), basename-exact so a hyphen-suffixed lookalike like `tg-foo` does NOT match; a path-qualified head (`/opt/homebrew/bin/tg`, `./tg`) does NOT match either — deliberately, since accepting any path would over-grant for this allow-direction check (unlike gh's deny-direction path normalization below); omp-steer/tg-ctl/rig follow the same predicate shape. ALMOST ALL `gh` is DELEGATED to a subagent (Alex tg#7103): CI/PR verification (`gh pr checks/view`, `gh run`, `gh api`) and every other gh subcommand are a subagent's job, not inline orchestrator work. ONE narrow exception, restored (Alex tg#9977, agent-tools#159; narrowed to per-LINE by agent-tools#363 after an adversarial review found a per-segment grant let an unrecognized companion mutation, e.g. `gh ship 205; rm -rf /`, slip through unblocked): a genuinely UNCHAINED `gh ship <PR#>` (head gh, next token literally ship, next token a bare PR number — anything AFTER that, including further bare tokens, not just flags, is unrestricted — AND no `&&`/`;`/`||`/`|`/bare-`&`/newline anywhere on the line) is sanctioned for the orchestrator to run inline, same as a subagent — `gh ship` with no PR number, any non-numeric argument, or `gh ship <PR#>` sharing a line with anything else at all still delegates. Subagent commands (agent_id present — for omp, restored by the bridge from the child's own nested session file) are allowed regardless. WARN first, BLOCK on repeat within ORCH_THIN_TTL_S (900s). The message is structured TRIGGER (the exact rule + the offending segment(s)) / WHY / DO THIS (harness recipe + what is allowed inline) / EXCEPTION. Per-repo opt-out (repo owner, not the constrained agent): agent_hooks.orchestrator_only:false in rig.yaml or RIG_ORCHESTRATOR_ONLY=0 (default ON). Deny-by-default: no self-service bypass (ALLOW_ORCHESTRATOR_WORK env / `# orchestrator-ok:` sentinel removed); a would-be BLOCK consults RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_ORCHESTRATOR_STAYS_THIN with a written justification, which asks Telegram via trusted tg-ctl and allows ONLY on an approval tap (a blank/bare 1 denies). timeout_ms 960000 covers tg-ctl ask's 900s cap plus margin so a hung/unanswered ask can't race the dispatcher's descriptor-timeout kill into a silent on_error=open ALLOW; a CC settings entry launching cc_hook_bridge must set timeout >960s (the 600s CC default would preempt this). on_error=open.
